members.name: ability_word

notes: V: see the sheets sub_14028A474, sub_14028A8B0 and JobScreen_BuildJobTabRows.

name: ActionEntryWord
summary: The 16-bit word of a four-byte action entry (the AI and preview form): the action id in bits 0..9 and the acting unit slot in bits 10..15. The current-action builder splits it with a 10-bit mask and a shift of ten.

members.name: action_id
members.text: Item id, ability id or throw item id depending on the command; the builder masks it with 0x3FF.

members.name: acting_unit
members.text: Acting unit slot, taken by a right shift of ten. A width census labels these six bits an action kind; the decoded reader uses them as the unit slot, and the record follows the reader.

behavior.text: the entry is four bytes: this word, a command byte and a flags byte. The builder stores the command byte at block +0, the word at +2 and the flags at +0x10.
only ten id bits are ever read, so a raw id above 1023 cannot reach the builder through this word.
for the Item command the word holds an ability id (item + 0x80) at use; the builder subtracts 0x80 to recover the item id, stores the item at block +6 and keeps the ability in the word.
for Throw the low ten bits are an item id first and become the resolved throw ability, so the word and the item field at +6 disagree about what the low bits mean until the ability is resolved.
a six-bit field cannot be both a unit slot and an action kind; the unit-slot reading is the decoded one, so the kind label in the width census is a naming error rather than a second meaning.

notes: V: the sheet Action_BuildCurrentAction (layout and the item/throw branches).
open_questions: ? whether any other producer packs a different field into bits 10..15 (the width census's kind).

name: ActionResult
summary: The result of one action on one target, filled by the formula handler and read by the result applier, the preview and the messages. One lives at +0x1BE of each battle unit record (g_BattleActionBlock points at the target's); a second, the caster's own result, is a separate static block (g_BattleCasterResult). Battle_ResultReset sets it up before the handler runs: hit flag 1, hit percent 100, nearly everything else 0.

members.name: hit
members.text: 1 = the effect lands, 0 = nothing happens. Battle_ResultReset stores 1; every miss path stores 0 (Formula_EvadeByteRoll, Formula_ChanceRoll, Formula_ZeroResult, Formula_StealGate).

members.name: critical
members.text: Set to 1 by Formula_CritRoll.

members.name: miss_reason
members.text: The reason when hit is 0: 1..4 an evade by evade byte k (Formula_EvadeRoll), 5 nullified (Formula_ZeroResult), 6 failed the chance roll (Formula_ChanceRoll, Formula_BardDancerGate), 7 no effect, 8 the caster-side katana result (Formula_DrawOutGate on the caster's block), 9, 11 and 13 reaction results. The meaning of each reason for the messages is I.

members.name: item_id
members.text: The picked equipment id of a steal or break (Action_PickTargetEquipment); on the caster's block the caster's word +0x1A8 (Formula_DrawOutGate).

members.name: hp_damage
members.text: HP damage (Formula_DamageAB; about 70 sites). Held at 0x7FFF by Formula_DamageAB and clamped to 999 by sub_14030A11C.

members.name: hp_heal
members.text: HP heal (Formula_HealSwap, Formula_DrainHP, Formula_FinalizeAbsorb).

members.name: mp_damage
members.text: MP damage (Formula_DrainMP and the MP formulas).

members.name: mp_heal
members.text: MP heal (Formula_DrainMP on the caster's block, the MP restore formulas).

members.name: gil
members.text: Gil change: the caster's block +gil, the target's block -gil (Formula_StealGilApply).

members.name: reaction_id
members.text: The reaction ability id to run after the result (440, 448..452 in the stock formulas 42 and 99 and in sub_14030AFEC).

members.name: flags
members.text: Flag word: 0x0002 recruit, 0x0004 equipment broken, 0x0008 draw-out kept, 0x0010 equipment stolen, 0x0040 status result, 0x0080, 0x0100 level drain, 0x0200 inflict roll passed (Formula_StatusChance19), 0x0400 absorbed (Formula_ElementAffinity), 0x0800 weak (doubled), 0x1000 draw-out katana broken, 0x2000 action failed banner, 0x4000 knockback present (Formula_KnockbackCalc). Stored by Formula_ElementAffinity, Formula_FinalizeAbsorb, Formula_StatusChance19, Formula_KnockbackCalc, Formula_56_StatusOnlyApplication and formulas 20, 37, 38, 46, 87, 88, 89.

members.name: speed_delta
members.text: A stat change: bit 7 = increase, the low 7 bits the amount. Written by formulas 57, 28 (ability 88), 29 (ability 95) and Formula_SapStatPick (143, 197). Which of +0x14 / +0x16 / +0x17 the game applies as which stat is I (the stock abilities that write each are known).

members.name: ct_delta
members.text: CT change: 0xFF = +127, 127 = -127 (formulas 18, 21, 93, 28 ability 92, 29 ability 99, 42 ability 117).

members.name: pa_delta
members.text: PA change (formulas 54, 85, 59; 28 ability 89; 29 ability 96; Formula_SapStatPick 144 / 198): Battle_ApplyActionResult applies it to the PA base +0x38 through Unit_ChangeBattleStat (cap 99, min 1).

members.name: ma_delta
members.text: MA change (formulas 86, 59; 28 ability 90; 29 ability 97; Formula_SapStatPick 145 / 199): applied to the MA base +0x39 through Unit_ChangeBattleStat (cap 99, min 1).

members.name: brave_delta
members.text: Brave change (formulas 58, 59, 97, 98 and 42 abilities 118 / 119).

members.name: faith_delta
members.text: Faith change (formula 42 abilities 120 / 121).

members.name: action_class
members.text: Stored by Battle_ResolveAction from dword_140787F84[2 * ability id] & 3, with 0x80 added when bit 0x1000000 of that dword is set, before the handler runs. Its meaning is ?.

members.name: equipment_slot_mask
members.text: The picked equipment slot of a steal or break: 0x80 head, 0x40 body, 0x20 accessory, 0x10 right weapon, 0x08 right shield, 0x04 left weapon, 0x02 left shield (Action_PickTargetEquipment; Formula_StealGate clears it).

members.name: status_add
members.text: The statuses to add: status s is bit 0x80 >> (s & 7) of byte s >> 3 (Formula_56_StatusOnlyApplication; sub_1403067D0 adds a bit in byte +0x1E).

members.name: status_remove
members.text: The statuses to remove (the name Status_FilterPendingSets gives the set at +34..38; bit 0x10 of the inflict flag copies the record into it). Formula_ElementAffinity sets bit 0x80 of byte +0x24 (I: status 16, Oil, so a doubled hit takes Oil away).

members.name: kind_bits
members.text: Result-kind bits: 0x80 HP damage, 0x40 HP heal, 0x20 MP damage, 0x10 MP heal, 0x08 status change pending, 0x01 another change (stat, gil, CT, EXP). Every routing block sets the matching bit with the amount.

members.name: reaction_copy
members.text: A copy of the reaction ability id (formula 99 writes 450 here and at +0x10); read by the message and reaction code.

members.name: exp_delta
members.text: EXP change: the amount ORed with 0x80 on the target's block (Formula_40_StealEXP).

members.name: hit_percent
members.text: The hit percent the preview shows and sub_14030A11C tests for 0 (it then clears the hit flag). Battle_ResultReset stores 100; Formula_EvadeRoll, Formula_BardDancerGate, Formula_ChanceRoll and Formula_56_StatusOnlyApplication scale it.

behavior.text: Battle_ResultReset (0x14030A410) clears the word at +1, the qword at +4 (+4..+0x0B), the dword at +0x0C, the qword at +0x12 (+0x12..+0x19), the word at +0x1A (+0x1A, +0x1B), the byte at +0x1C and the kind byte +0x27, stores 0x00640000 over the dword at +0x2A (hit percent 100) and 1 at +0, then calls sub_14030A43C, which clears the two status sets (+0x1D..+0x26) and a five-byte array at 0x14186B028. Not cleared: +0x03, the reaction id +0x10 and the copy +0x28 (so everything else is 0 after the reset except these three bytes).

Battle_ResolveAction resets both the target's block (g_BattleActionBlock) and the caster's static block (g_BattleCasterResult) before it runs the handler, so a handler may write the caster's own result without clearing it first.
the block is 0x30 bytes: the next field of the battle unit record after it is at +0x1EE (read as flag bits by sub_14030A11C).

after the handler (and sub_1403067D0 for ids below 7) sub_14030A11C(1) clamps the four amounts to 999, scales HP and MP damage by the difficulty row, runs the post hook of 12 formulas and clears the hit flag when the hit percent is 0; Battle_ResolveAction then ORs 1 into the kind byte (+0x27) when the flag word (+0x12) is non-zero (0x140309F84..0x140309F8B).
Unit_ChangeBattleStat applies +0x14 to Speed (+0x3A, cap 50), +0x15 to CT (+0x41), +0x16 to PA (+0x38), +0x17 to MA (+0x39), +0x18 to Brave (+0x2B), +0x19 to Faith (+0x2D).

notes: Read 2026-11-12. Offsets are relative to the start of the block, which is unit +0x1BE. The status sets and the array at 0x14186B028 are cleared by the reset through sub_14030A43C; the reaction id (+0x10) is not cleared by it.
open_questions: ? the meaning of +0x1A (action_class) and of the bytes +0x03, +0x1C, +0x28, +0x29 and +0x2B; what the five-byte array at 0x14186B028 holds (I: a staging copy of the pending status set).

name: AiCommandEntry
summary: One candidate action of the AI's command table: the ability word (id | unit slot << 10), the command (skillset) byte it comes from and a flag byte. A row of 34 entries per AI unit lives in g_AiCommandTable; the byte +2 = 0xFF of the entry after the last one ends the row.

members.name: word
members.text: The ability id in the low bits, the unit's slot << 10 above it (sub_140316D24 writes id | slot << 10, or slot << 10 alone for an entry with no ability, such as the Arithmeticks and Jump entries).

members.name: command
members.text: The command (skillset) byte the entry came from: 1 for the plain action of sub_140316B04's first entry, the unit's set for sub_140316D24's entries; 0xFF ends the row.

members.name: flags
members.text: Entry flags: the last entry holds 0x84 here (the word 0x84A9 stored at +2); sub_140316D24 sets bit 0x08 for the fourth list ability of a monster set (0xB0..0xDF) and clears it for the others. The other bits were not read.

behavior.text: the table is word_141872598 (g_AiCommandTable): 16 rows x 34 entries x 4 bytes, the row chosen by byte_141873038[unit slot]; an 8-byte header per row sits at byte_141872E20 (the item id word at header +4 is read by sub_140316D24 for the command kind 10 test).

sub_140316B04 writes entry 0 (command 1, word = slot << 10), then calls sub_140316D24 for the primary and (outside the monster range 0xB0..0xDF) the secondary set, then writes the last entry (word = (slot << 10) + 367, bytes +2 / +3 = 0xA9 / 0x84) and the 0xFF terminator when fewer than 34 entries are used.
readers of the command byte: 0x140320569, Ai_SurveyTargets (0x14031FED7), sub_14038D65C (0x14038D835); sub_140275EF4 (0x140276076) copies byte +2 to a unit's +0x13.

notes: Source: IDA reads of 2026-11-12. The row-header bytes other than the item word were not read.
open_questions: ? what a row header's bytes mean beyond the item word at +4; the readers of the table (sub_14038BC00, sub_14038C8F8, sub_14038D65C) were not read for this record.

name: AtlasShelf
summary: The state of one layer atlas allocator (a shelf / row packer): the cursor in the current row, the start of the row, the height of the row and the page. The UI manager holds two, the primary at +8616 and the secondary (masked layers only) at +8632; UIRender_PrepareLayers resets both every frame, GUILayer_PackAtlasRect and AtlasShelf_Alloc advance them.

members.name: cursor_x
members.text: Next free x in the current row (0 at the start of a page and of a row). Advances by the padded width plus the alignment pad.

members.name: row_y
members.text: Top of the current row (0 at the start of a page). Grows by the row height when a row is closed.

members.name: row_height
members.text: Height of the tallest rectangle in the current row, margins and alignment pad included; 0 for a new row.

members.name: page
members.text: Page index (0 at the start of the frame); +1 each time a rectangle does not fit below the current row.

behavior.text: the starting state of both shelves is {0, 0, 0, 0}: UIRender_PrepareLayers and the UI renderer constructor copy the zero pair g_ZeroPair into cursor_x / row_y and clear the row height (the page index is cleared by the same stores).

the primary shelf read {674, 239, 251, 4}: page 4, row top 239, row height 251, cursor 674. That is the state after the last layer of the list (slot 62, integer rectangle 610 x 187, margin 32, the first layer of its row: cursor 0 + 610 + 64 = 674, row top 239, row height 187 + 64 = 251); a model of the placement reproduces the whole state. The secondary shelf read {0, 0, 0, 0} (no masked layer in the frame).

notes: Detail and evidence: the function sheets linked from this page.

name: BattleMsgDescriptor
summary: The 4-dword descriptor the banner takes: class, subtype, kind and a message word. The banner resolves it to a template through a class/subtype switch; class 0 subtype 2 turns the kind and the word's low 11 bits into a table-172 message id, class 1 subtype 27 is a UI text id and class 1 subtype 171 a table-172 key.

members.name: class
members.text: 0 or 1 in the studied code. The text resolver switches on this together with the subtype (V, decompile).

members.name: subtype
members.text: 2 (event-script message id), 27 (UI text id) or 171 (direct table-172 key) in the studied code (V, decompile).

members.name: kind
members.text: Message kind. For class 0 subtype 2 it is the multiplier of the 1000-wide message-id base; only the kinds in registry BattleMsgKindBase give an id (V, decompile).

members.name: word
members.text: Message word, read as a u16 and masked with 0x7FF: the row index below the kind's base, or a table-172 key for class 1 subtype 171 (V, decompile and live trace).

behavior.basis: (live trace 2026-10-31, tracepoint on the banner function, one call during an ability cast)

behavior.text: 0x5062 packs group 10 in bits 11 and up and index 98 in the low 11 bits, an event-script message.
whether the traced call was produced by the ability cast. The code that builds the banner descriptor for an ability cast is not identified.

notes: V: a producer of descriptors of this shape is the scene task SceneMsgTask_Run. It reads the current scene task record's u16 at +28 as the word, takes group = word >> 11 to select one of the group objects at qword_140D40990, uses index = word & 0x7FF, asks the group object (sub_1400FC85C) for class and kind, and passes the descriptor to sub_1400EF9EC / sub_1400E5F78. I: its role in battle presentation follows the descriptor shape only; that it feeds the banner is not established (?).
open_questions: ? the producer of the descriptor the banner shows for an ability cast; ? how a scene task message reaches the banner, if it does.

name: BattleMsgEntry
summary: One slot of the battle message store: the kind, the kind-dependent argument, a message id and a 512-byte text buffer. The store is 40 entries at 0x20C stride after the message object's +8 (20,960 bytes); the dispatcher fills a slot and the resolver reads it back.

members.name: kind
members.text: Message kind (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9 and above were read). Kinds 4 and 9 resolve an item name; kind 6 an ability name.

members.name: arg
members.text: Kind-dependent argument: a number (kind 1), a unit record or battle unit index (2, 3), an item id (4, masked with 0x7FF; 9), an ability id (6), or an id + 0xB7C4 (7).

members.name: message_id
members.text: The kind-6 resolver stores id + 10000 here, a table-172 message id; no other writer was read.

members.name: text
members.text: The resolved text buffer: the resolver copies a name or a message into it (cap 511) and returns this address.

behavior.text: an entry is 0x20C bytes from the message object's +8; a slot above 0x27 returns null, so the store is 40 entries (20,960 bytes).
the dispatcher writes the kind and the argument; the kind setters (kinds 1, 3, 6, 9) write +0 and +4; the resolver writes +0xC and, for kind 6, +8.
Battle_Init clears 0x51E0 bytes at the object's +8, the whole store.

the argument filler reads the same storage as one flat record (struct BattleMsgRecord), so its dword offsets run across entry boundaries; this per-entry view is the one the setters and the resolver use.

notes: V: the store sits at g_BattleMsgObject + 8. The text buffer is the entry's exact remainder (0x20C - 0xC = 0x200 = 512 bytes).
open_questions: ? the use of +8 outside kind 6; ? whether every kind uses +4 the same way.

name: BattleMsgRecord
summary: The record the message object holds at +8: the values the argument filler reads for a message. Only the fields the filler touches are known; the names and roles below are inferred from that use.

members.name: kind
members.text: Selector matched against 4 and 9 when the message needs an item name (argument filler).

members.name: actor_index
members.text: Index into g_BattleUnitTable (512-byte stride); the filler reads the unit's data through it. Its low 11 bits are the item id when kind is 4.

members.name: name
members.text: Actor or record name used as a string argument. Length and encoding not established.

members.name: field_214
members.text: Read for some message ids; meaning not established.

members.name: fields_218
members.text: A run of dwords read from here for some message ids; count and meaning not established.

members.name: field_41C
members.text: Read for some message ids; meaning not established.

members.name: field_4184
members.text: Read for some message ids; meaning not established.

behavior.text: the offsets are the dword indices the filler uses (0, 1, 3, 133, 134.., 263, 4193) times 4; the fields the filler does not read are not listed.

notes: V: Battle_Init clears 0x51E0 bytes at the message object's +8. I: that block is the record storage, so the record is at most 20960 bytes. ?: the record's exact size and the fields between the listed offsets.
open_questions: ? the meaning of +0x214, +0x218, +0x41C and +0x4184; ? the name string's length and encoding.

name: BattlePanelHandWord
summary: One hand word as the flag-aware panels read it: the item id in bits 0..8 and a two-bit value in bits 14..15. The carrier is a 64-byte copy of a party or battle record's +0x30..+0x6F, at 0x141876E90 (field) or 0x141D3B880 (battle), with the five words at +0x24; it is not a field at unit+0x1EC.

members.name: item_id
members.text: Item id of the slot, masked with 0x1FF by the panel loops (0x14032F160, 0x140399E0C). 0xFF means empty and a value of 0x105 or more ends the walk.

members.name: slot_flags
members.text: Two-bit value taken with shift 12 and mask 0xC (shr 0xC at 0x14032F178/0x140399E24, and 0xC at 0x14032F17D/0x140399E29) and stored in dword_14184B228 / dword_140D40978. On the session carriers only bit 15 is ever set; bit 14 exists on the shop/menu list entries.

members.name: unused
members.text: No reader uses them; I: padding between the 9-bit panel id and the two flags.

behavior.text: the panels walk five words at carrier +0x24 (0x141876EB4 / 0x141D3B8A4), not at unit+0x1EC. The carrier is a copy: JobScreen_RefreshAfterChange copies record +0x30..+0x6F to 0x141876E90 (0x1402BD15D), PartyUnit_ReloadEquipment copies the live words to +0x24 (0x1402BDB42), and sub_14033E394 copies a battle record to 0x141D3B880 (0x14033E412).
two panel variants extract the top two bits: sub_14032EDB8 (task 9 over g_EquipCandidates, task 10 over 0x141876E90) and sub_140399A64 (over 0x141D3B880).
the id field is nine bits here, narrower than the party hand word, so the panel caps the id at 511 even before the flags are considered.

name: BattleSnapshot
summary: The 668,112-byte battle image a kind-1 resume entry carries, as the capture builds it in g_BattleState: a battle context, five blocks (A..E), the 21 x 512-byte unit records and 3,000 more bytes of scene-task state. Only the unit records hold object ids in bulk; the blocks are copied byte for byte and most of the image is never written.

members.name: context
members.text: Battle entry context: a pointer plus seven scene variables and an argument dword.

members.name: sub_object_1
members.text: Set up by a constructor call during the capture; shape not decoded.

members.name: sub_object_2
members.text: A 1 KB sub-object built by the same constructor; 45 nonzero bytes in the observed capture.

members.name: block_a
members.text: A 10,240-byte event-script file image (the buffer at 0x140D3CD50); item and job ids appear only as operands inside the script bytecode.

members.name: block_b
members.text: 887 u16 values: a per-map word table built from 24-byte static map records and indexed by scene variable 39; identical in all 24 payloads checked.

members.name: unit_records
members.text: 21 x 512 bytes from g_BattleUnitTable: job at +3, skillsets at +18/+19, abilities at +20/+22/+24, seven item words at +26..+39, name key at +508.

members.name: block_c
members.text: 512 eight-byte tile records of the battle map, indexed x + y * width; flag and movement-cost bytes only.

members.name: extra_capture
members.text: 3,000 bytes copied from 0x14114A4F0: 12-byte-ish entries with fill words; no id field identified.

members.name: block_d
members.text: Nine 168-byte scene-task data slots at 0x14114B150; captured but never restored.

members.name: no_work_copy
members.text: No slot work copy ends the snapshot: from +0x994EC the bytes are zero in every observed battle entry (no slot header), and block E lies inside that range at +0xA0418. An earlier reading that the last 40,164 bytes repeat the work copy was wrong.

members.name: block_e
members.text: The battle action state at 0x1418716A0: the current action word at +2 (an ability id masked to 10 bits), unit and action flags, and the wide action tables.

behavior.text: the capture writes 32 intervals, not the whole image; the largest never-written span is 501,656 bytes, so those bytes keep what an earlier battle left there and are still copied back on load.
the restore reads 117 sites; block D has no restore site and is reloaded by the scene-task path instead of from the image.
the only item ids are the 147 equipment words of the 21 unit records; the action word stores an ability id and an item use derives the item as the action number minus 128.
the image holds absolute pointers (the context pointer and a heap pointer at the start of the body), so it is a same-build snapshot and not a portable format.
blocks A, B, D and E carry no object id of their own because their writers are scene, map and action code rather than item or job stores; block C is a tile table.

notes: An earlier reading placed block E at 0x9F418. The capture's destination for 0x1418716A0 lands at g_BattleState + 0xA0418 and ends exactly where the tail fields begin, so 0xA0418 is the block and the older offset is 4,100 bytes of stale data.
open_questions: ? the shape of the 20 x 512-byte block at 0x3D51 (zero in the observed capture); ? the role of the 3,000-byte capture; ? the id content of block B's high bits and of block E's inner tables.

name: BattleTileRecord
summary: One tile of the battle map in g_BattleTileTable: 256 records per layer, two layers (layer 1 at +0x800), index x + y * width. Only the bytes the reach and target code reads are listed.

members.name: surface
members.text: Low 6 bits 0x3F: BattleRange_FlagTargetTiles never flags the tile (I: no surface, e.g. an unused layer-1 record).

members.name: height
members.text: Counted twice in the half-step heights of the reach rules (I: the height in whole steps; the HUD 'Height' agrees).

members.name: slope_depth
members.text: Bits 0..4 add to the half-step height; bits 5..7 times 2 add to a target's height and only conditionally to the attacker's (Unit_GetReachHeight). I: bits 0..4 slope / half step, bits 5..7 water depth.

members.name: corners
members.text: Four 2-bit fields, one per edge (shift 0 = the +x edge, 2 = -x, 4 = -y, 6 = +y): the edge's height is 2 * height + slope * field in half-steps (the move-range builder). (corners & 5) equal to 1 or 4 marks a one-axis slope for Battle_MoveRange_InitTiles.

members.name: flags5
members.text: Bit 0x40 set by BattleRange_FlagTargetTiles on the targetable tiles (I: the yellow mark). Bit 0x20 = a lit Move tile, written by Battle_MoveRange_Commit (live, 2026-11-05 and the 2026-11-09 captures). Low 5 bits: the tile's thickness in height steps; its underside is 2 * (height - thickness) half-steps (Battle_MoveRange_CeilingAbove).

members.name: flags6
members.text: Bit 0x01: BattleRange_FlagTargetTiles skips the tile; bit 0x02: BattleRange_MarkWeaponReach clears its weapon mark. Meaning ?.

behavior.text: the reach code reads it through g_BattleTileTable + 8 * (x + y * width + 256 * layer), width and height from g_BattleMapSize.

notes: Detail and evidence: the function sheets linked from this page.
open_questions: ? bytes +1 and +7 (not read by the reach or move-range code).

name: EquipPanelBlock
summary: A 64-byte copy of a party or battle record's bytes +0x30..+0x6F, kept at 0x141876E90 for the field equip screens and at 0x141D3B880 for the battle panels. Its five hand words sit at +0x24 (record +0x54) and a second five-word array at +0x2E (record +0x5E). It is a screen copy, not a field of the unit record.

members.name: record_30
members.text: Copy of record +0x30..+0x3F. Filled by JobScreen_RefreshAfterChange (0x1402BD15D) and sub_1402BBBCC (0x1402BBF68) with movaps; by PartyUnit_ReloadEquipment (0x1402BDB20) from record B +0x30.

members.name: record_40
members.text: Copy of record +0x40..+0x4F in the screen writers. PartyUnit_ReloadEquipment overwrites the whole 16 bytes with a local value whose low word is the two-handed result (0x1402BDB37).

members.name: record_50
members.text: Copy of record +0x50..+0x5F; its words at +0x24..+0x2C are the five hand words.

members.name: hands
members.text: The five equipment words at record +0x54..+0x5C. PartyUnit_ReloadEquipment copies them raw from g_PartyUnits (movsd at 0x1402BDABB, word at 0x1402BDAB7, movaps to +0x24 at 0x1402BDB42); JobScreen_RefreshAfterChange and sub_1402BBBCC copy record +0x30..+0x6F with movaps, which carries +0x54..+0x5C to +0x24..+0x2C.

members.name: second_row
members.text: Five words at record +0x5E..+0x66; read by sub_14032F410 (0x14032F4D3) and sub_14032F9F8 (0x14032FCEC). ? who fills them; they are not the hand words.

members.name: record_68
members.text: Copy of record +0x68..+0x6F.

behavior.text: the field copy is written by PartyUnit_ReloadEquipment (0x141876E90), JobScreen_RefreshAfterChange (0x141876E90) and sub_1402BBBCC (0x141876E90); the battle copy is written by sub_14033E394 (0x141D3B880).
the two panel readers extract bits 14..15 of the hand word with shift 12 and mask 0xC: sub_14032EDB8 at 0x14032F178/0x14032F17D and sub_140399A64 at 0x140399E24/0x140399E29.
the id is masked with 0x1FF by both panel readers, so the panel's id field is nine bits wide even though the source party word uses ten.

notes: V: the 0x141D3B880 layout is the same 0x30..0x6F copy, written by sub_14033E394 from a battle record.
open_questions: ? the source battle record of sub_14033E394 and whether a flagged party word can still be in it when a battle panel opens.

members.name: stat_word_04

members.name: stat_words_06
members.text: Four stat words cleared at 0x140286BF7 and read by sub_1402C20F0 (0x1402C24C7-0x1402C24E4) as the attack/defence pair it shows.

members.name: mode_word
members.text: The panel variants test it for zero: sub_14032EDB8 at 0x14032EE8B (alias 0x141876C4E) and sub_14032F410 at 0x14032F4DA. Zero selects the one-row layout, non-zero the two-item layout.

members.name: two_handed
members.text: 0 or 1 from sub_140284998: 1 when the selected hand weapon is two-handed or carries the record byte's bit 4. Written at 0x1402D5DE8, 0x1402D6A34, 0x1403340A2 and 0x14036C35B; read by sub_14032EDB8 (0x14032EE84) and sub_14036BBFC (0x14036BD23).

members.name: stat_words_12
members.text: Four stat words cleared at 0x140286C02; sub_1402C20F0 reads the pair at +0x16/+0x18 (0x1402C2479, 0x1402C24A5) and the pair at +0x20/+0x22 (0x1402C2486, 0x1402C24B2).

members.name: stat_words_1C

members.name: candidates
members.text: The five candidate equipment words (g_EquipCandidates, 0x141876C64..0x141876C6D). Bits 0..9 are the id; bit 15 marks a proposed change; 0 is empty. The builder marks only the first four; the fifth (word at +0x2C) is copied from the unit's +0x5C by the session functions.

members.text: Five words read by sub_14032F410 (0x14032F4D3/0x14032F4C0) as a second row of item ids. No instruction in the .text census writes them; ? writer and meaning.

members.name: tail
members.text: No reader or writer found in the exported set; ? content.

behavior.text: the block is one 0x40-byte object; g_EquipCandidates is its +0x24 field, not a separate array (0x141876C40 + 0x24 = 0x141876C64).
sub_14028728C and sub_140287354 fill only the stat words and read the equipment words masked with 0x3FF; neither writes the candidate or display words.
sub_140287D9C marks four candidate words with 0x8000 (loop count four at 0x140288471) and leaves the fifth to its callers.

notes: V: addresses and writers from a census of the sites; the stat field names are descriptive only, the pair order was not decoded.

members.text: A copy of the weapon's 8-byte record, made by Mem_CopyChecked with size 8 (0x140309BC5 and 0x140309D39).

the capture buffer of Battle_SaveCapture / Battle_RestoreCapture keeps the formula byte at buffer +0x48; a wider formula id would change that layout.
the block's two bytes +0x17 and +0x18 are one word at 0x1407B0787 for the stores at 0x140309BDB (0x0100) and the reads of +0x17 through `byte word_1407B0787`.

the weapon and chemist formula bytes come from the copied records of the same resolve (ability record +8 at the ability branch, weapon record +2, chemist record +0): the block keeps only the clamped result at +0x18, plus the weapon record copy that Formula_106 reads.

name: GUILayer
summary: A UI layer: a component drawn offscreen and composited with its effects (mask, drop shadow, glow). Fields as read by the layer passes.

members.name: index
members.text: Layer index: selects its 4-vertex slot (64 bytes) in the shared layer quad buffers.

members.name: sort_lo
members.text: The layer's order (initially its index; UIRender_PrepareLayers renumbers it): its low 9 bits are the lowest field of the sort key of every command of the layer.

members.name: sort_hi
members.text: The layer's atlas page (GUILayer_PackAtlasRect writes it, -1 before): its low 6 bits go into the sort key above the pass field.

members.name: atlas_page
members.text: The page of the secondary atlas of a masked layer (GUILayer_PackAtlasRect, +487 layers only; -1 otherwise). Read as the page-change marker by UIRender_PrepareLayers.

members.name: layer_kind
members.text: Layer kind 0 / 1 / 2 (the prepare and submit paths test it against 2).

members.name: blend_mode
members.text: Selector digit 0 of the final blit (the layer blend).

members.name: tex_slot_a
members.text: Texture slot the passes bind their first source to.

members.name: tex_slot_b
members.text: Texture slot of the second source.

members.name: used
members.text: Set by UIRender_AppendCommand when a draw command is appended to the layer, cleared per frame (UIRender_ClearLayerFlags); only used layers are collected, packed and composited.

members.name: culled
members.text: Set by UIRender_PrepareLayers for a layer with a source layer (+489) whose rectangle does not overlap it; a culled layer draws and blits nothing.

members.name: effect_flags
members.text: Effect group enables +176 (single float group), +177 (drop shadow), +178 (glow); +486 the +178 context group, +487 the mask layer flag, +488 unused, +489 the mask source flag.

members.name: composited
members.text: 1 after GUILayer_ResetRecord (the dword 0x01000000 written at +176), cleared only for a layer drawn by a kind 10 node (GUINode_DrawKind10); GUILayer_Composite and the atlas packer run the layer passes only when it is set.

members.name: int_rect
members.text: The layer's integer screen rectangle x0, y0, x1, y1 = (int)x, (int)y, (int)(x + w), (int)(y + h) of the rectangle before packing (GUILayer_PackAtlasRect); the scissor of the layer blit.

members.name: packed
members.text: 1 when the layer has its own rectangle in an atlas page (GUILayer_PackAtlasRect: composited, kind 0 or 1, and the +78, +486 and +488 flags clear); the offsets +0xE0 are 0 otherwise.

members.name: cbuffer_slot
members.text: Constant-buffer slot the layer's constants are bound to (UILayer_FillConstants binds the layer buffer at RenderContext.cbuffer_handles[this]).

members.name: offset_vectors
members.text: Three offset vectors; the blit picks a selector variant when any is non-zero.

members.name: single_radius
members.text: Radius of the single-float effect group (UIB value x min scale, written by GUILayer_BuildRecord when +176 is 1). GUILayer_ExpandBounds adds it to the blur reach when +176 is set; GUILayer_PackAtlasRect uses it above 3.2 for the wide margin.

members.name: shadow_strength
members.text: Drop-shadow strength (constant row 13).

members.name: shadow_radius
members.text: Drop-shadow blur radius in target pixels (= UIB radius x min(scale x, scale y)); the blur sigma.

members.name: shadow_offset
members.text: Drop-shadow offset in target pixels (UIB offset x scale per axis); constant row 12.zw, added to the shadow quad.

members.name: glow_strength
members.text: Glow strength.

members.name: glow_radius
members.text: Glow blur radius.

members.name: rect
members.text: Layer rectangle x, y, w, h in the space of its render target (the effect atlas).

members.name: atlas_offset
members.text: Offset between the layer's rectangle in the atlas and its place on the parent target: screen position = rect - atlas_offset.

members.name: shadow_colour
members.text: Drop-shadow colour (constant row 31).

members.name: glow_mode
members.text: Glow shader mode (3 on the Job Tree).

members.name: blur_radius
members.text: Radius of the whole-layer blur group (kind 1 layers; UIB comp+188 x min scale, written by GUILayer_BuildRecord when the ctx+184 flag is set). GUILayer_ExpandBounds adds it to the blur reach when the kind dword (+28) is 1; GUILayer_PackAtlasRect uses it above 3.2 for the wide margin.

members.name: target
members.text: The layer's render target object (UILayer_GetTarget); layers are 592-byte objects in an array of the UI renderer.

behavior.text: live (Job Tree, 1280 x 720): the name tag layer reads strength 0.5, radius 0.8, offset (1.6, 1.6), rect (457, 2, 130, 94), atlas offset (296, -377); the title layer radius 2.0, offset (0, 2.667), strength 1.
a layer whose glow, effect or shadow radius exceeds 3.2 gets the wide margin when its atlas rectangle is packed (rect and atlas_offset are written there).

behavior.basis: (live read 2026-10-30, 58 layers of a running screen)
behavior.text: layer_kind 0 for every layer but one whole-layer blur layer (kind 1); blend_mode 0 for most, 2 (multiply) on the Lv chips, 7 on one; the last layer holds the full 1280 x 720 rectangle.

notes: Detail and evidence: the function sheets linked from this page.

name: GUINodeState
summary: One state (timeline) of a component: its clock, its loop range, its flags and the channel sets and entries it applies. Created by GUINode_NewState from a 208-byte pool slot, filled by GUIComponent_LoadDef / UIAnim_PlayStateTracks, started by GUINode_PlayState, advanced by GUINodeState_Advance and applied by GUIComponent_ApplyStateAnims. The states of a component are the vector at component +616 .. +624.

members.name: name_key
members.text: The state's name (UIName_Assign / UIName_SetKey); GUINode_FindState matches the interned id at +8.

members.name: transition_key
members.text: Set by GUIComponent_LoadDef from the state record; when its id at +0x18 is non-zero GUIComponent_ApplyStateAnims applies a previous state first, and passes this key to the component lookup.

members.name: prev_component
members.text: Component of the previous state (the own component when its id at +0x28 is 0).

members.name: prev_state
members.text: Name of the previous state (the state's own name when its id at +0x38 is 0).

members.name: transition_delay
members.text: Frames before the transition's state applies: the previous state is sampled at (time - delay) once time >= delay.

members.name: record_flags
members.text: Written from the state record's int at +4 by GUIComponent_LoadDef; -1 in a fresh object. What reads it is not known.

members.name: rate
members.text: Clock multiplier, 1.0 in a fresh object; GUINodeState_Advance adds dt * rate to time.

members.name: time
members.text: Clock in seconds. GUINodeState_Advance: time = (dt * rate) + time; a loop or jump sets it to target / 60.0.

members.name: frame
members.text: Current frame = time * 60.0, a float (not an integer count). GUIComponent_ApplyStateAnims samples every active state at this value; for a state driven by a link GUIAddon_OnStateEvent writes it.

members.name: prev_frame
members.text: The frame at the previous tick (the jump-marker and keyframe-event tests compare against it); equals frame when the state did not advance.

members.name: frame_count
members.text: Frames of the state (the record's +28), the loop end when the range is unset.

members.name: range_start
members.text: Loop range start; the range counts only when range_start < range_end, otherwise the range is 0 .. frame_count.

members.name: range_end
members.text: Loop range end.

members.name: enabled
members.text: 1 = the state takes part in GUINode_UpdateStates and GUIComponent_ApplyStateAnims. 1 in a fresh object; GUINode_StopState clears it.

members.name: running
members.text: Set by GUINode_PlayState; GUINodeState_Advance advances only while it is set and clears it at a non-looping end.

members.name: dirty
members.text: Set by GUINode_PlayState and by the link writer; cleared by GUINodeState_Advance. While set GUINodeState_IsPastEnd answers false.

members.name: paused
members.text: 1 = the clock does not advance (a parent link drives the frame). GUINode_PlayState on a paused state only clears it.

members.name: loop
members.text: 1 = at the end frame the state restarts at the range start. From the UIB record's byte +32 at load; UIAddonFingerCursor_PlayLoop sets it for the cursor's Loop.

members.name: keep_alive
members.text: GUINode_UpdateStates keeps advancing a state that is past its end while this is set; the rest of its meaning is open.

members.name: hold
members.text: 1 = the state does not advance and counts as past its end (GUINodeState_IsPastEnd); cleared by GUINode_PlayState.

members.name: absolute
members.text: 1 = sampled values replace the node's fields, 0 = they are combined with them. 1 for every state loaded from a UIB timeline.

members.name: created
members.text: Set to 1 by GUINode_NewState; its reader was not found.

members.name: owners
members.text: Owner ids that receive the state's events (GUIOwners_PostEvent). GUINode_NewState puts the component's own id here.

members.name: channels
members.text: One channel set per target node (begin +0x90, end +0x98): the key tracks GUINode_ApplyAnimChannels samples (track pointers a[6] .. a[31]).

members.name: entries
members.text: Begin +0xB0, end +0xB8: the jump markers, triggers, state links and resets of the state.

members.name: field_C8
members.text: Zero in a fresh object; no reader found.

behavior.text: a fresh object is 1.0 at +0x48, enabled (+0x68 = 1), everything else zero except +0x44 = -1 (GUINodeState_Alloc).
the clock rule is in the behavior UIStateClock; the bob of the finger cursor is in CursorGloveBob.

notes: Detail and evidence: the function sheets linked from this page.
open_questions: ? +0x44, +0x6D, +0x70 and +0xC8; the meaning of the three transition keys is inferred from their use in GUIComponent_ApplyStateAnims.

name: GUINodeStateEntry
summary: One entry of a state's entry list (GUINodeState.entries): a jump marker, a trigger, a state link, a state reset or a part trigger, built from the state's special tracks by UIAnim_ApplyTrack and UIAnim_ApplyComponentTrack.

members.name: type
members.text: 1 jump marker (tag 5031), 2 / 3 / 4 triggers (tags 5032 / 5033 / 5034), 5 state link (5028), 6 state reset (5029), 7 part trigger (5030).

members.name: track_id
members.text: The id of the track in the UIB file.

members.name: start_frame
members.text: The track's start frame. Jump marker: the frame jumped to. State link: the parent frame that maps to child frame 0.

members.name: end_frame
members.text: Start frame + the track's duration. Jump marker: playing past it jumps to start_frame. State link: the parent frame that maps to the child's last frame.

members.name: target_name
members.text: Types 5, 6, 7: the target node's name (the node holding the child component).

members.name: child_state
members.text: Types 5 and 6: the child state's name.

members.name: value
members.text: Types 2, 3, 4, 7: the id passed to the trigger.

members.name: value2
members.text: Type 4: the number at value block +84 times 256 (GUIAddon_OnStateEvent multiplies it by 1/256).

behavior.text: GUINodeState_Advance posts event 40 for every entry whose type is not 1 and whose start and end frames differ on every tick (a span entry), and for a point entry on the tick its frame is passed.

notes: Detail and evidence: the function sheets linked from this page.
open_questions: ? Whether 2 / 3 / 4 are sound and voice triggers (inferred from their use only).

name: HdSheetGroup
summary: One of the 20 sheet groups of the battle HD layer (g_HdSheetGroups): a sheet entry kept in memory and the textures cut from it, one per piece and palette.

members.name: index
members.text: The group's own number (HdLayer_BuildTextures writes it before it uses the group).

members.name: pieces
members.text: Rectangles of the sheet's pieces, 20 bytes each (x, y, width, height first): a draw record names one by its dword +72. I: the count follows from the space up to +2692.

members.name: entry
members.text: The g2d entry the buffer holds; a draw record with another entry frees the group's textures and reads the new one.

members.name: pixels
members.text: The entry's bytes (0x80000 bytes, allocated once and zeroed).

members.name: textures
members.text: 144 bytes each: a texture object, then at +112 the palette hash, +116 in use, +120 the age (60 when used, counted down), +124..+136 the piece's x, y, width, height.

members.name: count
members.text: Number of textures made in the group.

behavior.text: groups 15 to 17 are built with 256 palette colours and 8-bit pixels, every other group with 16 colours and 4-bit pixels (HdLayer_BuildTextures passes the pixel width to HdGroup_BuildPiece).

name: HdTextureId
summary: One row of the EventSpriteHdTextures table and the tables that share its shape.

members.name: texture_id
members.text: HD texture id used for that event sprite (-1 = none); a second texture id = this + 140

name: IdRemapRow
summary: Seven id pairs.

members.name: pairs
members.text: Seven (from, to) pairs: the lookup returns the to of the first pair whose from matches; a to of -1 means none; ids up to 0xA7 pass through unchanged.

name: ImportSlotRow

name: InputActionRow
summary: One action of the input module (g_InputModule + 1360 + 48 * action id, 256 rows; ids are UIKeyAssign keys): three 16-byte bindings, the pad button first, then two keys. The offsets below are of the pad binding; the key bindings repeat them at +16 and +32.

members.name: binding
members.text: Low word: pad button id (first binding) or key code (second and third); flag 0x10000 long press, 0x20000 short press; 0 = unbound.

members.name: press_time
members.text: UI clock (ms) when the value last rose from 0.

members.name: value
members.text: Current value, 0 or 100 for a button (a trigger or stick gives 0..100).

members.name: value_copy
members.text: Second copy of the value; its previous content decides 'released'.

members.name: pressed
members.text: 1 on the frame the button went down (Input_IsActionMapped and Input_TestAction's keyboard fallback read it).

members.name: released
members.text: 1 on the frame it is no longer held after a non-zero value.

members.name: held
members.text: 1 while the button is down (Input_IsActionHeld reads it).

members.name: held_copy
members.text: Written with the same value as held (pad binding).

members.name: repeat
members.text: Auto-repeat pulse (sub_1400F0D98 reads it).

behavior.text: refreshed every frame by Input_UpdateActionRow; a row whose context bit is not in the module's mask (+13720) reads all zero.

row 89 = key 17 (Ctrl), alternate key 164 (fifth mouse button), pad button 18 (RB): the fast-forward hold. Row 90 = key 53 (the 5 key), pad button 30 (Y while row 89 is held): fast-forward level 2. Row 91 = key 16 (Shift), pad button 15 (X): the auto-advance toggle. Rows 93 / 94 = key 32, pad 13 (the skip hold), row 95 = key 27, pad 23 (pause).
the only writer found of the context mask stores 0x15 at start-up (sub_1400F159C), so the default context bit 1 is always present.

notes: Detail and evidence: the function sheets linked from this page.
open_questions: ? Which of the three UIKeyAssign pad columns is copied for the current button layout (row 89 has a pad id only in the second column).

members.name: key_states
members.text: Key states at +576 + 4 * key code; bit 0 = down. Keys 16, 17 and 18 (Shift, Ctrl, Alt) are read directly at +640, +644 and +648 (InputKey_ReadBinding).

summary: The analog part of the 0x548-byte input state that the UI listeners receive (copied whole by sub_1400EFB50 and by GUICore_OnInputState): four signed stick bytes, two trigger bytes and the button dwords.

members.name: left_stick_x
members.text: Seen live 2026-11-10 (virtual pad sticks, each axis both ways). -100 .. 100 after the dead zone (Pad_ReadSticks out[0]). Read as the free pointer's horizontal axis.

members.name: left_stick_y
members.text: Seen live 2026-11-10 (virtual pad sticks, each axis both ways). Pad_ReadSticks out[1]; FreeCursor_StepFromSticks uses it negated as the pointer's vertical step.

members.name: right_stick_x
members.text: Seen live 2026-11-10 (virtual pad sticks, each axis both ways). Pad_ReadSticks out[2]; ListScroll_HandleStick scrolls a horizontal bar with it.

members.name: right_stick_y
members.text: Read by ListScroll_HandleStick and UIGadgetFFTOVScrollText_HandleScrollInput as the vertical scroll axis (the order of the four bytes is Pad_ReadSticks' output order).

members.name: left_trigger
members.text: 0 .. 100 (Pad_Poll out[4]); tested with the sticks by sub_1400F0BC8.

members.name: right_trigger
members.text: 0 .. 100 (Pad_Poll out[5]).

members.name: button_bits_a
members.text: Button mask read by sub_1400F02BC (id 17 = bit 8 LB, 18 = bit 11 RB, 21 = bit 10, 22 = bit 13 ...; bits per Input_UpdateActionRow). Which dword is held and which is new is not settled.

members.name: button_bits_b
members.text: The second button dword read in the same way.

behavior.text: seen live 2026-11-10: in the input module object (`qword_143CD9EE8`) this struct starts at +8: the sticks are at module +0x4D0 LX, +0x4D1 LY, +0x4D2 RX, +0x4D3 RY, signed -100 .. 100 after the dead zone, Y positive when pushed up (a full push reads 100 / -99).

a scan of every instruction with a displacement of 1224 .. 1227 (2026-11-10) finds no JobTree_* function: the Job Tree reads only its eight direction bytes (JobTree_HandleInput) and the confirm / cancel actions, so both sticks and both triggers are unused on that screen.
GUICore_OnInputState reads all four stick bytes (raw event 26, 'pad axes') and the free-pointer handler FreeCursor_StepFromSticks reads the left stick; ListScroll_HandleStick reads the right stick.

behavior.text: cell i is at static object 0x1418716A0 + 2*i; the object pointer is 0x141871698, set once at startup by sub_1403166C0. 17 word readers in 10 functions and 9 word writers in 3 functions were read, all 16-bit; no 32-bit per-cell field exists.
two near-identical builders (sub_14023678C and sub_1402EA58C) write 0x3800 | id or 0x7000 | id; a value of 8 goes to a separate static array (0x140D492D0), not to the cell array.
the object is rebuilt per list build, never allocated or freed, and has no length header (the build count is a local; the visible window is held in two words, 0x1407831B0 and 0x1407831B2).

published views: 0x1407831C0 = the object, 0x1407831C8 = object + 0xA4, 0x1407831D0 = object + 0x148, 0x1407831D8 = the separate static array. 0x14184A9B0 is an alias of the object pointer, written through by 11 task functions.
the 11 id bits are the text-id index field, so the 0x800 ceiling of format TextId applies to a cell; the cell cannot carry a 16-bit item id.

notes: V: object address 0x1418716A0; the highest field used is +0x385 and no label marks the end of the buffer.
open_questions: ? the roles of the property word and the five byte arrays; ? the object's exact size; ? which screen builds cells with the 0x7000 tag (ability cells).

name: ItemNewFlagBlock
summary: The block at g_ItemNewFlags: the shop new-item flags first, then the four Poachers' Den (poach) arrays. The last poach byte is at +0x3EE; g_InventoryCounts begins at +0x3F0, one byte later. The save serialises the five parts from this base and the code addresses the poach parts by literal offsets from it.

members.name: shop_new
members.text: Two flag bytes per item id 0..260. One plane is cleared when the item is first sold and the other when it is first obtained (I: the shop badges).

members.name: poach_item_num
members.text: Poach stock count per poach item id; the reader in sub_1400D6FB0 stops at 96.

members.name: poach_item_get_order
members.text: Obtain order of the poach items, read by sub_1401ABE14.

members.name: poach_item_sort
members.text: Sort position used by the poach list.

members.name: poach_item_new
members.text: Two flag bytes per poach item, set to the pair 0x01 0x01 at a new game; the last byte is +0x3EE.

behavior.text: the shop/poach serialiser writes five descriptors from this base: 261 flag pairs at 0, then the 97-byte count, obtain-order and sort arrays at 522, 619 and 716, then the 97 flag pairs at 813.
the save work pack and unpack copy the whole 1007-byte block, and every poach reader and writer uses its literal offset from this base.
the new-game reset writes the shop flag pairs to the pair 0x01 0x01, then clears the three 97-byte poach arrays and sets the 97 poach flag pairs to the same value.
only 272 bytes separate the Poachers' Den stock from this base (0x1411A7700 to 0x1411A7810), so the 261-byte den array cannot grow in place either.

notes: V: the save and poach functions.
open_questions: ? whether the two shop flag planes mean "new in this shop" and "new to the party" as inferred from the clear sites; no code names them. ? the byte at +0x3EF between the last poach flag pair and the inventory counts; no reader and no save field names it.

name: ItemOrderLists
summary: The ten saved item order lists: 16-bit words in static storage, no header and no length word. Five item-menu lists (A0..A4) sit in scattered arrays reached through one pointer table; five equip and obtain-order lists (B0..B3 and B4) form one contiguous block. The save carries A as five copies and B as one 1010-byte copy.

members.name: item_user_sort
members.text: Item-menu order, group 0 (weapons and shields). Live at 0x1407B2550, 282 bytes; 139 stock ids can enter it, so two entries are spare.

members.name: item_user_sort2
members.text: Item-menu order, head. Live at 0x1407B2678, 60 bytes; 29 stock ids, one spare.

members.name: item_user_sort3
members.text: Item-menu order, body. Live at 0x1407B24B0, 76 bytes; 37 stock ids, one spare.

members.name: item_user_sort4
members.text: Item-menu order, accessory. Live at 0x1407B2500, 68 bytes; 33 stock ids, one spare.

members.name: item_user_sort5
members.text: Item-menu order, thrown weapons. Live at 0x1407B26B8, 42 bytes; six stock ids, fifteen spare.

members.name: equip_user_sort_hand
members.text: Equip-screen order for the hand, with the same membership as the first item-menu list. Live at 0x141874540.

members.name: equip_user_sort_head
members.text: Equip-screen order for the head. Live at 0x14187465A.

members.name: equip_user_sort_armor
members.text: Equip-screen order for the body. Live at 0x141874696.

members.name: equip_user_sort_accessory
members.text: Equip-screen order for the accessory slot. Live at 0x1418746E2.

members.name: item_get_order_sort
members.text: Obtain order, the only list with the whole id range as its membership. Live at 0x141874726, 524 bytes; 258 stock ids, four spare.

behavior.text: the end of every list is a word equal to 0xFF (255) or at least 0x105 (261). Ids 0..254 and 256..260 are therefore storable and only 255 is not, although 0xFFFF is the terminator of the separate menu list.
no list stores a length. The initialiser writes the 0xFF terminator into all ten, zeroes the whole B block from a zeroed 1010-byte template and then rewrites six of the eight sort-field byte lists.

the five A lists are reached through the pointer table at 0x14067F498 (a second table at 0x140689C38 holds the same five pointers); the B lists through the table at 0x14067FA90, and the obtain-order list starts 0x1E6 bytes into the block.

the membership writers insert a newly owned id at index 0 and shift the tail right with no capacity check. A3 ends flush against the mode-1 sort bytes and A1 has only two spare words before A4, so one word too many changes a neighbour rather than a spare entry.

the save pack writes A0..A4 as five fixed-size copies at 0x8A6C, 0x8B86, 0x8BC2, 0x8C0E and 0x8C52, and the whole B block as one 1010-byte copy at 0x8C7C; the load and the repair pass read the same six.
a second syncer (sub_14039684C) maintains the same lists from the inventory snapshot instead of the live counts, and reaches the obtain-order writer by a tail jump.
the stock id counts (139, 29, 37, 33, 6 and 258) leave 2, 1, 1, 1, 15 and 4 spare, so a stock save cannot exercise the insert-without-capacity path.

notes: V: the list table, the save copies, the initialiser and the adjacency, with the sheets of the eleven writers and copiers.
open_questions: ? the purpose of the 12-byte table at 0x1407B26F0 that the initialiser writes next to the lists; no order-list function reads it.

Seven functions test it: ShopEntry_Fill, sub_140332C54, sub_140332C8C, sub_140336664, sub_14036A994, sub_140366FE0, sub_140333974.

members.name: not_current_equipment
members.text: Not set on g_MenuList. The only function that sets it is sub_140287D9C (0x140288544), on its four-word output buffer (g_EquipCandidates), not on this array; sub_1402875A4 has no 0x8000 immediate, and no g_MenuList reader tests bit 15.

members.name: terminator
members.text: Ends the list; this array uses 0xFFFF, unlike the ten saved order lists, which end at 0xFF.

behavior.text: the same 256-word array is reused by four list kinds: shop (Shop_BuildItemList), equip (Inventory_BuildEquipList), ability (JobAbilityList_Build, sub_140286A78) and item/equip pages (sub_14036C3EC).
31 exported functions hold 49 instructions that name the array: 41 load its address with lea (as an output list or a callee argument) and 8 read an entry directly.
a builder stops at 145 entries and writes the 0xFFFF terminator; the insert path of the sorter stops at 146.

the array is rebuilt whenever a screen opens and is never saved, but sub_140285F2C copies its words into the saved order list off_14067F498[group] and sub_140336B88 copies a stack list into off_14067FA90, both without stripping flag bits.

notes: V: the sheets of the builders, the row helpers and the two movers.
open_questions: ? who reads bit 12 or bit 13 of an ability entry; ? whether a flagged word can reach off_14067F498 through sub_140285F2C in a running screen (the one caller builds the list in mode 0, so no flagged word was seen on that path).

members.name: mode
members.text: File header byte 8: 1 single key, 2 double, 3 triple.

members.name: last_key

name: PartyHandWord
summary: One equipment slot of a party unit: the item id in bits 0..9 and bit 15 as the Outfitter-session pending flag. Five of them sit at g_PartyUnits +0x54..+0x5C, one per slot.

members.name: item_id
members.text: Item id of the slot. Most consumers mask the word with 0x3FF; some compare the raw word (Item_CountEquippedByParty at 0x1402874D8, ShopEntry_Fill at 0x14036B4A3), so a flagged word is not seen as the same item there.

members.name: session_pending
members.text: Set on a slot changed in the current Outfitter/shop session: sub_1402D7280 sets it when it stores id | 0x8000 and adds the price to dword_143D1AC68 (0x1402D733A), and the apply loops copy a bit-15 candidate into the word. The commit handler sub_1402D65D4 strips it before the save is written. It is not the item-present flag: a committed item keeps the id with this bit clear.

members.name: cannot_equip
members.text: Produced on list entries by Inventory_BuildEquipList (bts 0xE at 0x140288CAF) and Shop_BuildItemList (or 0x4000 at 0x140288FBD/0x140289061). sub_1402D7280 refuses a candidate that carries it (bt 0xE at 0x1402D72A0); sub_1402D5B6C and sub_1402D65D4 test it as part of a >= 0x4000 comparison. No stock writer sets it on a party word.

members.name: unused
members.text: No writer sets them; sub_1402D65D4's 0x3FF strip would clear them on a word at or above 0x4000, but a word in 0x0400..0x3FFF is not stripped. I: padding between the 10-bit id and the two flag bits.

behavior.text: five words per party unit, at +0x54, +0x56, +0x58, +0x5A and +0x5C of the party record; 0 is empty, not 0xFF.
a word at or above 0x8000 is treated as session-pending and its price is already in dword_143D1AC68; a word below 0x8000 is a plain 16-bit id and may still carry bit 14.
the bit and the id share one 16-bit word, so the store cannot hold a 16-bit id without moving the session flag out of the word.

notes: V: layout, writers and readers come from the sheets sub_1402D6FB8, sub_1402D7280, sub_1402D6464, sub_1402D65D4 and sub_1402D5B6C. The earlier 'present' reading of bit 15 was wrong: the commit path strips it from an item that stays equipped.
open_questions: ? whether any session teardown other than the commit/cancel messages can leave bit 15 set on a party word.

name: PostBattleCalc
summary: The per-formula post-processing object of a battle: a virtual function table pointer and 106 rows of 32 bytes, one per formula id, that sub_14030A11C runs after a formula handler. Twelve rows hold a callback (an Undead rule); the rest hold the do-nothing marker. Allocated and filled in Battle_Init (the pointer is g_PostBattleCalc).

members.name: vftable
members.text: vftable_ffto::Game::Battle::PostBattleCalc_140713F28 (0x140713F28), stored by Battle_Init right after the 0xD48-byte allocation.

members.name: rows
members.text: Row n - 1 at 0x08 + 32 * (n - 1) belongs to formula id n; sub_14030A11C reads the row of the clamped formula byte when it is below 107, so formula ids above 106 have none.

behavior.text: 0xD48 = 8 + 106 x 32; sub_1401F92A8 fills the rows from a stack template of 106 rows with a 0x6A-iteration copy loop (Battle_Init, 0x14020F004).
the object is the argument of every hook row, so a callback receives the object in rcx (the thunk sub_14001B9D8 jumps through [rdx], the row's callback field).

notes: Source: IDA reads of 2026-11-12. The rows' callbacks: see PostBattleCalcRow.
open_questions: ? what the other virtual functions of the table do (the object is used only through its row array here).

name: RenderContext
summary: The per-thread draw state every pass fills before it packs a command: sort key, clip rectangle, render target, blend and raster words, vertex/index buffers and three binding tables (constant buffers, textures, sampler words) indexed by registry slot ids. members.text: Clip rectangle x0, y0, x1, y1 (reset to unbounded); the layer passes copy the layer's rectangle here and set the clip-enable bit in raster_word.

members.name: target

members.name: blend_state
members.text: Blend state word (low bits kept across the reset, the rest from an engine constant).

members.name: raster_word

members.text: Blend word of render target 0 (programs can override it; see blend_rt1_7).

members.text: Flag word: draw type bits, bits 9..11 the number of extra blend words.

members.name: index_buffer
members.text: Index buffer object.

members.name: input_layout
members.text: Vertex input layout object of the draw (about 15 passes set it; RenderState_PackCommand sizes the vertex-buffer table from its +52).

members.name: target_handle
members.text: Render-target binding of the draw (handle of target).

members.name: shader_stages
members.text: Shader object per stage, written by ShaderProgram_ApplyState (+0x98 + 8 x stage); RenderState_PackCommand walks the five entries.

members.name: vertex_buffers
members.text: Vertex buffer k: handle at +0xC8 + 16k, stride at +0xD0 + 16k, byte offset at +0xD4 + 16k.

members.name: cbuffer_handles
members.text: Constant-buffer handles indexed by constant-buffer slot id.

members.name: texture_handles
members.text: Texture handles indexed by texture slot id.

members.name: sampler_words
members.text: Packed sampler word per sampler slot id (registry SamplerSlots); decoded into a D3D12 sampler by Sampler_DescFromWord. Reset to the engine default word every frame.

members.name: blend_rt1_7
members.text: Blend words of render targets 1..7 (BlendDesc_FromWords). The per-program words ShaderProgram_ApplyState copies go to blend_rt0 and here.

members.name: blend_factor
members.text: Blend factor colour (reset to 1.0).

members.name: blend_factor_mask
members.text: Bit i: render target i's blend word uses the blend factor (ShaderProgram_ApplyState sets it from the word's factor fields); when non-zero RenderState_PackCommand appends blend_factor to the command.

members.text: Size of the packed vertex-buffer table cache; RenderState_PackCommand rebuilds the cache when the pointer is 0 or the size differs.

members.name: vb_cache
members.text: Packed vertex-buffer table cache; the passes set it to 0 when they change vertex buffers.

members.name: pack_object
members.text: Read by RenderState_PackCommand (its +40 is copied into the command); zeroed by the reset. Role open.

behavior.text: RenderContext_ResetFrame rewrites every context at the start of a frame; all 64 sampler words become the default word (0 at runtime: point filter, wrap).
a pass sets only the fields it needs and inherits the rest from whatever the context holds when it packs its command (see the flow FrameUiSubmission).

name: SaveManager
summary: The two singletons the save path runs on, with the fields it uses: the save-I/O state object that holds the frame step's command and sub-state, and the save manager object that holds the 50-slot image the `fftsave.bin` payload is built from. The offsets below name the object each field belongs to.

members.name: command
members.text: The step the frame step will run: 1 store, 2 load, 3 image to cache (0 idle).

members.name: sub_state
members.text: Phase of the current step: its progress inside the case the frame step is running.

members.name: image
members.text: The 50-slot image, 2,008,200 bytes: the payload of `fftsave.bin` on a store and the source of the cache after a load (1528 decimal).

members.name: game_save_data
members.text: The GameSaveData sub-object the entry queue writes into (904 decimal).

behavior.text: the frame step reads the command from the save-I/O state object and runs one case; the UI callbacks only set the command, so the screen never touches the container.
the image is a mirror of the cache: a store copies the cache into it, a load copies it back (2,008,200 bytes), so the two always hold the same 50 slots.
the sub-state is a phase counter rather than a retry count, because a step that finishes clears the command instead of incrementing it.

notes: The save-I/O state object is qword_140D405B8 and the manager is qword_143CD9EE0; the request object qword_140C69698 is a third object (SaveRequestRecord).
open_questions: ? the other fields of the save-I/O state object, and whether +0x108 is ever nonzero at the start of a frame.

name: SaveRequestRecord
summary: One queued file request of the save container manager: the consumer object, the entry name, the delivery buffer and its status. The queue is a vector on qword_140C69698 (first +0x40, last +0x48) of 328-byte (0x148) records, guarded by the critical section at +0x10 of the same object.

members.name: size
members.text: Size of the delivered payload (the entry minus its 16-byte header).

members.name: data
members.text: The delivered payload; the delivery allocates it with the record's heap.

members.name: heap
members.text: Allocator the delivery copies the payload with.

members.name: obj
members.text: The object the entry is delivered to: its +624 buffer and +632 size receive the payload.

members.name: name
members.text: Entry name, NUL-terminated; this is what the read kick filters on.

members.name: flag
members.text: Handed to the delivery call unchanged (0 in the requests observed).

members.name: status
members.text: Delivery status; 0 on the normal path.

behavior.text: a read request is pushed by sub_140033CBC with the object and the name, and served by sub_140033DF0, which copies the entry's 16-byte header into the object, calls the object's handler, then runs the object's post-delivery step.
the records are contiguous at stride 328 between the vector's first and last pointers, so a service can walk first..last and compact the ones it served.
the same queue carries the manual slot request (`fftsave.bin`), the settings request and every autosave entry, so one read kick serves them all.
a request that no kick serves stays queued until a later load or until the object is destroyed.

notes: The queue object also holds the busy flag at +392 and a byte at +602 that is cleared before a request, so a request made while a container write is in flight returns an error string.
open_questions: ? the flag at +0x120 (0 in every request seen); ? whether an unserved record is ever removed by the game itself.

name: UnitSpritePosePackRow

members.name: header

name: UnitWorkRecord
summary: The working copy of a unit: the 21 battle units (g_BattleUnits) and temporary copies for previews and the job screens. Same per-job arrays as the save record at other offsets.

members.name: marker
members.text: Copied from the save record +0.

members.name: slot_id
members.text: The unit's slot id (save record +1).

members.name: job
members.text: Job id.

members.name: innate_words
members.text: Four innate ability words (+0x0A, +0x0C, +0x0E, +0x10); Unit_BuildAbilityBits passes each to Unit_SetAbilityBit.

members.name: equipped_reaction
members.text: The equipped reaction ability id; Unit_SetAbilityBit also writes it for any reaction-range id (below 454).

members.name: equipped_support
members.text: The equipped support ability id (Unit_BuildAbilityBits sets its bit).

members.name: equipped_movement
members.text: The equipped movement ability id (Unit_BuildAbilityBits sets its bit).

members.name: head
members.text: Equipped item, 0xFF = none (UnitWork_ApplyStartingEquipment: setup byte 18, default picked with slot bit 0x20; I: head).

members.name: body
members.text: Equipped item, 0xFF = none (setup byte 19, slot bit 0x10; I: body).

members.name: accessory
members.text: Equipped item, 0xFF = none (setup byte 20, slot bit 0x08); Unit_LoadEquipmentAndEvade reads its accessory sub-record.

members.name: right_weapon
members.text: Weapon of the first hand, 0xFF = none: UnitWork_ApplyStartingEquipment puts the first hand item here when it is not a shield; BattleRange_MarkWeaponReach takes the Attack weapon from here first; Unit_LoadEquipmentAndEvade copies its power / evade to +0x44 / +0x46. I: the right hand (Status lists it first).

members.name: right_shield
members.text: Shield of the first hand, 0xFF = none (the first hand item when its slot bits have 0x40).

members.name: left_weapon
members.text: Weapon of the second hand, 0xFF = none; the Attack weapon when +0x20 is empty; cleared when the first weapon's flags have bit 0x01 or +0x9A bit 0x02.

members.name: left_shield
members.text: Shield of the second hand, 0xFF = none.

members.name: pa_base
members.text: PA before equipment: Unit_ComputeStats writes it in mode 0; Unit_ChangeBattleStat moves it within 1..99 for the PA change of an action (result block +0x16) and keeps the total +0x3E.

members.name: ma_base
members.text: MA before equipment (result block +0x17 changes it, 1..99).

members.name: speed_base
members.text: Speed before equipment (result block +0x14 changes it, 1..50).

members.name: stat_bonus
members.text: PA, MA, Speed from the attribute records of the equipped items (Unit_ApplyEquipment zeroes and sums them).

members.name: pa_total
members.text: PA = min(+0x38 + +0x3B, 99) (the last loop of Unit_ApplyEquipment; Unit_ChangeBattleStat keeps it).

members.name: speed_total
members.text: Speed = min(+0x3A + +0x3D, 50): the CT gain Battle_TurnEngine phase 0 adds to +0x41 each tick (halved by Slow, x1.5 by Haste).

members.name: ct
members.text: CT: phase 0 adds the gain and clamps to 254; a unit acts at 100 or more (result block +0x15 changes it).

members.name: move
members.text: Move: Battle_MoveRangeSetup caps it at 124; the move range's start budget is move + 1.

members.name: jump
members.text: Jump: Battle_MoveRangeSetup caps it at 7; a step may differ by 2 * jump half-steps and a jump passes over jump / 2 tiles.

members.name: weapon_power
members.text: Weapon power of +0x20 / +0x24 (ItemWeaponRecord +4), written by Unit_LoadEquipmentAndEvade.

members.name: weapon_evade
members.text: Weapon evade of +0x20 / +0x24 (ItemWeaponRecord +5).

members.name: phys_evade
members.text: Accessory, first shield, second shield sub-record byte 0 (I: physical evade).

members.name: class_evade
members.text: JobTable byte 26 of the unit's job (Unit_LoadEquipmentAndEvade).

members.name: magic_evade
members.text: Accessory, first shield, second shield sub-record byte 1 (I: magic evade).

members.name: tile_x
members.text: Map tile x (the range builders seed from it).

members.name: tile_y
members.text: Map tile y.

members.name: layer_facing
members.text: Bit 7 = map layer of the unit's tile (Unit_GetReachHeight indexes the tile table with it); low bits facing (playbook, live).

members.name: status_16_23
members.text: Status bits 16..23, status s = bit 0x80 >> (s & 7): 0x40 (Float) raises the reach height; 0x02 (Toad) makes Attack use item 0.

members.name: spawn_byte_4
members.text: Copied from spawn entry +23 (Unit_ApplySpawnRecord); its meaning is not decoded.

members.name: side_presence
members.text: Copied from spawn entry +24 (also to +0x1EE): bits 0x30 = side, bits 0xC0 = presence at battle start (Battle_PlaceEntryUnits: 0x00 off the field unless a preview unit shares the marker, 0x40 one random bit decides, 0x80 placed, 0xC0 built and look queued but not on the field and not counted).

members.name: spawn_byte_28
members.text: From spawn entry +28 (above 99 = random 0..99).

members.name: level
members.text: Level, from spawn entry +3 by Unit_ApplySpawnRecord (clamped 1..99).

members.name: brave_base
members.text: Written from spawn entry +6 together with +0x2B (that +0x2A is a base copy is I).

members.name: brave
members.text: Brave (spawn entry +6; above 100 replaced by 45 + random 0..29).

members.name: faith_base
members.text: Written from spawn entry +7 together with +0x2D (that +0x2C is a base copy is I).

members.name: faith
members.text: Faith (spawn entry +7, same rule as Brave).

members.name: name_string
members.text: The unit's own name string (UnitWork_SetNameKey: save record +0xDC).

members.name: spawn_tail
members.text: Copied from spawn entry +33..+39 (Unit_ApplySpawnRecord).

members.name: spawn_flags
members.text: The spawn flag set: OverrideEntryData flag bytes as bits 0..10, stored by Battle_PlaceEntryUnits. Bit 0x04 = objective target (BattleObjective_ShowsTarget); bits 0x18 and 0x01 are read by the turn panel.

members.name: name_key
members.text: Name key (CharaName table), set by UnitWork_SetNameKey; read by CharaName_GetDisplayName callers.

members.name: ko_counter
members.text: The KO counter: Unit_SetStatusCountdown sets it to 3 when KO is applied (0xFF when +5 bit 2 or +6 bits 0x09 are set: the unit never crystallises); BTurn_OnTurnStartStatus counts it down at the turn start; at 0 the unit becomes a crystal or a chest.

members.name: innate_status_a
members.text: Status set (40 bits, status s = bit 0x80 >> (s & 7) of byte s >> 3): the statuses the unit always has = job row status_a | equipment status_a (UnitWork_ApplyJobRow, Unit_ReloadFromJobRow, Unit_ApplyEquipment). Timed statuses (24..39) in it never expire.

members.name: innate_status_b
members.text: Status set: the statuses the unit is immune to = job row status_b | equipment status_b. Status_FilterPendingSets drops them from a pending add; Unit_ReinitStatusCountdowns removes the always-on ones from it.

members.name: status_effective
members.text: The effective status set the behaviour code tests: always innate_status_a | applied_status (Battle_StatusApply, Battle_StatusRefresh, Unit_ReinitStatusCountdowns, Unit_ReloadFromJobRow all end with that OR). Byte 2 is status_16_23 below. A job row's status_c is copied here only until the next recompute.

members.name: status_countdown
members.text: Remaining duration (CT ticks) of the statuses 24..39, byte = id - 24: started from the property table (+3) by Unit_SetStatusCountdown, decremented once per engine pass for battle-applied, non-innate statuses (Battle_TurnEngine phase 4); Doom (byte 15) counts at the unit's turn start.

members.name: charge_counter
members.text: The remaining charge time of a Readying or Jumping unit (0xFF = none); Battle_StatusResolve sets 0xFF when none of Readying, Jumping, Performing is set.

members.name: pending_status_add
members.text: The statuses the action or event in progress wants to give (result block +29): written by the formulas, the turn-start rules, the tile effects and event opcode 0x92; consumed by Battle_StatusResolve and cleared by Battle_ResultResetStatusSets.

members.name: pending_status_remove
members.text: The statuses the action or event in progress wants to take away (result block +34); Status_FilterPendingSets limits it to applied statuses that are not innate.

members.name: applied_status
members.text: The statuses applied in battle: the only set Battle_StatusApply sets and Battle_StatusRefresh clears (the engine decrements the countdown of its timed members).

members.name: passive_bits
members.text: Passive-ability bit map, 88 bits for the ids 422..509 (bit 0x80 >> (index & 7) of byte +0x94 + (index >> 3), index = id - 422); the last three bytes (+0x9C..+0x9E) are the ones also listed below as move_flags_c, move_flags_d and move_flags.

members.name: passive_bits_halve_mp
members.text: Byte 5 of the passive map: bit 0x80 (id 462) halves the MP cost of an action (sub_1402828E4, sub_14030B1A0); bit 0x40 (id 463) is the JP Boost test of the JP award.

members.name: move_flags_c
members.text: Bit 0x02: Battle_MoveRangeSetup sets the jump to 31 (no height limit).

members.name: move_flags_d
members.text: Battle_MoveRangeSetup: bits 0x0C select Teleport (cleared for Toad / Chicken); 0x10 keeps the unit out of water; 0x02 makes the weather-dependent terrains cost 1; 0x01 makes every enterable terrain cost 1.

members.name: move_flags
members.text: Bit 0x08 raises the reach height like Float; bits 0x80 / 0x40 add the tile's water depth / depth - 2 (Unit_GetReachHeight). Battle_MoveRangeSetup picks the movement mode from it: 0x04 Fly, 0x08 float, 0x20, 0x80, 0x40, 0x10 the lava and water modes (record MoveRangeScratch). I: movement-ability flags.

members.name: unlock_mask
members.text: Unlock bits (Unit_AwardJobJp rebuilds them after an award).

members.name: learned
members.text: Learned-ability bits.

members.name: job_levels
members.text: Job level nibbles.

members.name: jp
members.text: Current JP (Unit_AwardJobJp adds to it).

members.name: total_jp
members.text: Total JP.

members.name: confirm_result
members.text: The result of the target-confirm shape routine (sub_140206F90): -1 drops the confirm, 0 or 1 opens the target confirmation (battle state 25), 2 starts the charge motion, 3 and above do nothing.

members.name: action_request
members.text: The unit's pending 20-byte action block (+1 command byte, +2 ability id u16). Only four direct stores write it (BattleAction_BuildUnitRequest 0x1402832AD, sub_1402831D8 0x140283235, Formula_37_RendEquipment 0x140307EB9 and its restore 0x140307EED); every other copy (the request queue, BattleAction_BuildReaction, BattleAction_ReleaseCharged, Battle_ExecuteSecondaryAction, BTurn_PreviewAction, the AI current action) is a call of Mem_CopyChecked with size 0x14. BTurn_PreviewAction saves and restores it around a preview.

members.name: action_command
members.text: The command (skillset) byte of the request (index into g_CommandKind; 18 = jump); TurnList_InsertEntry writes bit 0x20 of a turn entry when it is 18. A byte holds sets up to 253. The name token of the command is 0xB000 plus this byte (BattleMsg_UnitTurnScene 0x14023750F).

members.name: action_ability
members.text: The ability word of the request; the turn order and the action message read it; BTurn_PreviewAction restores the block.

members.name: mount
members.text: Bit 7: Unit_GetReachHeight adds 2 and reads the flags of the record at slot (low 5 bits). I: riding, the low bits the mount. Battle_MoveRangeSetup also reads bit 6 with the low 5 bits (a unit paired with the acting unit is not an obstacle).

members.name: side
members.text: Battle_MoveRangeSetup compares bits 0x30 of every other unit's byte +0x05 with this byte of the acting unit: different = the other side (an obstacle). I: the side the unit currently fights for.

behavior.text: UnitWork_CopySaveFields fills the arrays from a save record; UnitWork_StoreToSaveSlot writes them back.
the Toad restriction on abilities tests status byte +0x63 mask 0x02 (sub_1402828E4, sub_14030B1A0): a Toad unit may use only ability 0, 367 and 29 (a command kind of 10 never).
the passive-ability map is rebuilt by Unit_BuildAbilityBits; see PassiveAbilitiesAreAPerUnitBitMap.

name: WorldMapLocationRecord
summary: One 64-byte record per world-map location that the location-list builder accepts (location ids 0..46): what is on offer there and its state at the current story progress. The location info panel is filled from it.

members.name: errands_offered
members.text: Number of errands offered there (Errand_IsOffered over ids 0..95).

members.name: value_a
members.text: The location's entry of the first per-location array the builder fills (v88); the panel shows it as a counter.

members.name: value_b
members.text: The location's entry of the second per-location array (v89); the panel shows it as a counter.

members.name: no_open_errand
members.text: 1 when no errand record is open for the location; selects panel text 1583 or 1584 for a location without a shop.

members.name: category_mask
members.text: One flag per item category (Item record byte +5) that the location's shops sell (Shop_BuildItemList kinds 1, 2, 3, 4 and 7); filled only when Town has_shop is set. The panel plays 'On' / 'Off' on 35 nodes from it.

members.name: progress_state
members.text: 3 when the location is the current WorldMapProgressInfo row's town, 2 when it is town_2, else 0.

members.name: location_id
members.text: The location id (Town key).

members.name: sort_order
members.text: Town sort_order (+0x20); the three Locations lists are insertion-sorted by it, then by id.

members.name: byte_60
members.text: Set by the builder; meaning not decoded.

members.name: not_marked
members.text: 1 when the location is not marked.

members.name: poachers_den
members.text: Town poachers_den (+0x32) when event variable 144 is above 0.

behavior.text: the builder (sub_14036E5DC) pushes each record into the list for Town locations_list (+0x24): list 53 + value (values 0..2) or the separate list at +1696 for values above 2.
the first array entries (+4, +8) come from per-location values filled earlier in the same function; their meaning (the panel's counters) was not followed to the source.

notes: Sheets: sub_14036E5DC (the builder), WorldMapLocationPanel_Fill (the reader).
